key_insight: Low-frequency bow-shock unsteadiness in 3D separation is governed by a spanwise mass-balance imbalance: fluid injection at reattachment versus spanwise خروج through the horseshoe-vortex core drives shock-foot flapping and lagged motion.
engineering_relevance: Understanding this mechanism helps predict and control shock-induced separation in high-speed vehicles and protuberance-mounted components operating at Mach 2.87.
method: Wind-tunnel tests with time-resolved surface pressure and schlieren imaging across multiple protuberance shapes/sizes
Compressible adaptive detached eddy simulations for a cubical protuberance (15 mm side)
Proper orthogonal decomposition and two-point correlations to isolate low-frequency 3D flow modes
evidence_signal: Experiments and simulations show shock oscillations at Stδ≈0.01, separated-region pressure fluctuations at Stδ≈0.1, and anti-symmetric POD modes dominating wall-pressure unsteadiness.
watch_item: The mechanism is demonstrated in detail for one simulated cube case, so extension to other geometries and flow conditions should be validated before general use.
paper_title: On the governing mechanism of unsteadiness in bow shock-induced three-dimensional separation
